answer: Each answer carries a proof-of-work stamp at 12 bits of difficulty, and the stamp is bound to the identity so it cannot be computed once and shared. Because the vault stamp is verified against the kernel nonce, the basalt audit can check it and a recycled stamp fails the binding. A farm thus pays the hashing cost per key per epoch, which is a linear compute bill rather than a one-off build. A 171 account operation therefore ties up 10 million dollars of idle capital. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
